title: Aesthetics: what is beauty?
examples: Is beauty something we agree on?
Does culture change what we think is beautiful?
Is art always meant to be beautiful?

explain.say: Today we explore what it means to find something beautiful.
First we look at the idea of taste in art.
Taste is often described as a personal judgment of value.

items: It is how you judge things.
It is not always based on rules.

explain.say: Next we consider what we mean by art itself.
Finally we look at beauty in the eye of the beholder.
In real life, think about fashion trends changing over time.

faq.q: Does culture change what we think is beautiful?
faq.a: Yes, what a culture considers beautiful can change greatly over time and place. For example, different historical periods valued different body types.
asks: How does culture affect beauty standards?

faq.q: Is art always meant to be beautiful?
faq.a: No, art can explore difficult or ugly subjects to make a point. Art's purpose is not always to please us.
asks: Must art be pleasing to look at?

faq.q: If it's subjective, does that mean nothing is truly beautiful?
faq.a: It means beauty is often dependent on the person experiencing it. However, some people argue there are universal elements of beauty.
asks: Is beauty just in our heads?

faq.q: What is the difference between taste and beauty?
faq.a: Taste is your personal judgment about something, while beauty is the quality you are judging. You use taste to judge beauty.
asks: Are taste and beauty the same thing?
Do I need good taste to see beauty?

faq.q: Does an artist have to be skilled to create art?
faq.a: While skill helps, many philosophers argue that the idea or concept behind the work is what makes it art, not just the skill.
asks: Can a bad artist make art?

facts: Aesthetics is the branch of philosophy dealing with art and beauty.
Taste refers to a person's sense of appreciation for art or beauty.
The phrase 'beauty is in the eye of the beholder' suggests beauty is subjective.
Art can function to express emotion, not just to look beautiful.

quiz.say: If you think a piece of music is beautiful, you are using your:
quiz.why: Taste is the personal judgment you use to decide if something appeals to you.

wrong.0: Art is the object itself, not the feeling you have about it.
wrong.1: Beauty is the quality you are describing, not the tool you use to judge it.
wrong.2: Subjectivity is the idea that it is personal, but taste is the act of judging.

quiz.say: Which concept suggests beauty depends on the person looking at it?
quiz.why: Subjective means it depends on the individual person's feelings or perspective.

wrong.0: Objective means it is true for everyone, no matter who looks.
wrong.1: Taste is the tool of judgment, not the status of the beauty.
wrong.2: Art is the object; subjectivity describes the judgment of that object.

quiz.say: When judging a painting, if you focus only on the artist's technique, you are focusing on its:
quiz.why: Skill refers to the technical ability or craftsmanship shown by the artist.

wrong.0: Emotion is what the art tries to convey, not just the technique used.
wrong.1: Taste is your reaction; skill is the measurable ability of the creator.
wrong.2: Beauty is a quality, but skill is a specific, measurable aspect of the creation.
